findings.title: Async legacy write inherits request context and is cancelled
findings.body: Create (and Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) spawn `go func()` deriving the async context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` where `ctx` is the request context. When the API request completes the request context is cancelled, so the background legacy write is immediately cancelled / times out and legacy silently diverges from storage. The async context must be detached, e.g. derive from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` with values copied.

findings.title: Storage error recorded as legacy metric
findings.body: In `Create` when `d.Storage.Create` fails the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with the storage start time. The same mistake is in `Update` at line 129. Storage failures are therefore counted against legacy latency/error metrics and storage metrics miss the failure, corrupting dashboards/alerts for mode 3.

findings.title: Delete storage metric uses name as kind label
findings.body: In `Delete` the success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...)` passing the object name where the kind label is expected (error path correctly uses `options.Kind`). This creates high-cardinality / wrong kind labels for delete metrics.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage metric
findings.body: In `DeleteCollection` the async legacy goroutine calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` for the legacy call. It should call `d.recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors are attributed to storage and legacy metrics are never emitted.

findings.title: Delete installs wrong logger in context
findings.body: In `Delete` the code builds `log` with name/kind/method values but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. All other methods install the enriched `log`. Downstream storage/legacy calls from Delete lose the per-request fields.

findings.title: Async legacy write races on input object / objInfo
findings.body: The `go func()` closures capture and use `obj` in `Create` and `objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, options` in `Update` without a deep copy. The caller may mutate/reuse the object after return and `Storage.Create/Update` may mutate it in place, so the concurrent legacy write races with the caller and can write corrupted/divergent data. A copy must be made before spawning the goroutine, and the returned `created`/`res` object should be the source for legacy, not the pre-storage input.
